memorial_rites.title: Roll-Call Naming
memorial_rites.description: At the first morning muster following a demise, the deceased's name is called once in normal shift order, followed by three seconds of silence before the next name.

memorial_rites.title: The Unmade Bunk Night
memorial_rites.description: The deceased survivor's bunk is left untouched and unoccupied for twenty-four hours, with the wool blanket folded once at the footboard.

memorial_rites.title: The Small Tin Division
memorial_rites.description: The deceased's personal items—a pencil stub, a comb, a patched glove, an heirloom—are reviewed by close peers. One item is archived, others returned to storage with consent.

memorial_rites.title: The Final Shift Detail
memorial_rites.description: Close shift companions carry out the physical committal—burial in the rock crevice or sealing into the ash vault—working without conversation until the last bolt is tight.

memorial_rites.title: Memorial Wall Inscription
memorial_rites.description: The survivor's surname, trade specialty, and total days survived are chiseled into the limestone face of the shelter's lower gallery with a hardened center punch.

memorial_rites.title: The Spoken Wish Fulfillment
memorial_rites.description: If a Final Wish was recorded, its outcome is formally declared aloud before the shelter assembly, affirming that the community bore witness to their final request.
